comment: The draft correctly states that implementation fails for want of people and identifies specialist capabilities. The role model would be stronger if it more explicitly connected architectural accountability with clinical/professional semantic stewardship, clinical digital safety, information governance, cybersecurity, public engagement and AI oversight. Without named ownership, these functions may be treated as temporary project input rather than sustained national capability.

public.text: The draft correctly states that implementation fails for want of people and identifies specialist capabilities. The role model would be stronger if it more explicitly connected architectural accountability with clinical/professional semantic stewardship, clinical digital safety, information governance, cybersecurity, public engagement and AI oversight. Without named ownership, these functions may be treated as temporary project input rather than sustained national capability.
public.suggestedRevision: Within the non-prescriptive role model, explicitly require accountable capability for national architecture; clinical/professional leadership; nursing and other domain semantic stewardship; data standards and terminology management; clinical digital safety; privacy/data protection; cybersecurity and resilience; AI/algorithm governance; public and community engagement; procurement/lifecycle assurance; and evaluation. Countries may combine roles, but decision rights, deputies, escalation routes and RACI-style (responsible, accountable, consulted, informed) responsibilities should be documented.
